decisions.reason: The Definition explicitly says to use R_T(z)=(T-zI)^(-1); it does not identify that symbol with the supplier's (zI-T)^(-1). Since T-zI=-(zI-T), the local inverse is the negative of the supplied inverse on exactly the same resolvent set. With first-variable-linear inner product, every matrix element and its continuation acquire the same factor -1, leaving pole locations and orders unchanged. No supplier identity with a sign-sensitive numerator is invoked. The stated local convention is consistent and needs no repair.

The cited completeness theorem [F2] is stated for the unprojected strong limits, with exactly this real bounded compactly supported potential and H^2 realization, and already proves (a) and (b). Its V=0 specialization, explicitly permitted and computed as Omega_pm=I in local step 1.2, gives H_ac(H0)=ran I=H and hence P_ac(H0)=I. Independently, the same supplier's F1 supplies the free scalar spectral density rho_u(E)=sqrt(E)/2 times the sphere integral of |hat u(sqrt(E) omega)|^2, zero on E<=0; thus every free scalar measure is absolutely continuous. The projection in [F4] is therefore the identity, and both wave conventions and their products Omega_+^*Omega_- coincide. This is an immediate consequence of an existing cited supplier, not an unsatisfied prerequisite.
